title: The New Vaccine Surveillance Network: 25 years of active, population-based surveillance for pediatric infectious diseases in the United States.

title: Tick-Induced Mammalian Meat Allergy in Australia: National Prevalence and Geographic Distribution from Laboratory Surveillance, 2014-2024

analysis.background: The study aims to characterise the national epidemiology of tick‑induced mammalian meat allergy (MMA) in Australia, addressing the previously unknown scale, temporal trends, geographic distribution and risk factors of this tick‑borne IgE‑mediated condition (A1).
analysis.methods: A retrospective analysis of α‑Gal specific IgE ImmunoCAP™ test results from 1 Jan 2014 to 31 Dec 2024 was performed (A2); de‑identified records from 14,075 tested individuals across Australia were linked to SA3 postcodes (A3); a subset of 1,515 individuals with repeat testing enabled longitudinal assessment (A4); outcomes included test volumes, case counts, positivity rates, spatial clustering, demographic risk ratios and antibody trajectories (A5).
analysis.results: Overall 35.7% (5,025) of tested persons were positive (A6); testing volume rose 331% with case detection accelerating sharply from 2020 (A7); 59–81% of case growth was attributable to expanded testing, leaving a residual increase unexplained (A8); cases clustered along the eastern seaboard within the Ixodes holocyclus range, with three SA3 regions accounting for >25% of national cases (A9); females predominated and risk peaked at ages 45–74 years (A10); among repeat testers, α‑Gal sIgE levels declined predictably in 93% of people (A11).
analysis.contribution: The paper provides the first national assessment of MMA in Australia, revealing a substantial, geographically concentrated and growing burden (A12); it highlights that targeted public‑health actions in a few high‑incidence regions could efficiently reduce national disease impact (A13); and it demonstrates that serial sIgE testing can monitor clinical status, supporting ongoing risk mitigation (A15).
analysis.limitations: The authors note that while testing expansion drives most of the observed increase, prospective studies are needed to separate surveillance artefacts from true disease emergence (A14); the retrospective laboratory‑based design limits inference about clinical outcomes or causality.

analysis.summary_en: Background: The study aims to characterise the national epidemiology of tick‑induced mammalian meat allergy (MMA) in Australia, addressing its previously unknown scale and risk factors (A1). Methods: Retrospective analysis of α‑Gal sIgE ImmunoCAP™ results from 2014‑2024 on 14,075 individuals linked to SA3 postcodes, with 1,515 repeat testers for longitudinal analysis (A2‑A5). Results: 35.7% (5,025) tested positive; testing rose 331% with case detection accelerating from 2020; 59–81% of case growth due to expanded testing; cases clustered on the east coast, three SA3s >25% of cases; females predominated, risk peaked at 45‑74 years; 93% showed predictable antibody decline (A6‑A11). Contribution: First national MMA assessment showing a substantial, geographically concentrated, growing burden; suggests targeted interventions could efficiently reduce disease impact and supports serial testing for monitoring (A12‑A15). Limitations: Prospective studies are needed to disentangle surveillance effects from true emergence; retrospective lab data limit causal inference (A14).

title: Adaptive Evolution of Serotype O Foot‐and‐Mouth Disease Virus Under Vaccine Pressure: Combined VP1 T142/Q153 Mutations Drive Antigenic Alteration and Immune Evasion

analysis.background: Foot‑and‑mouth disease virus (FMDV) escapes host immune surveillance via adaptive evolution driven by vaccine‑mediated selective pressure, leading to persistent breakthrough infections in immunized animals.
analysis.methods: The dominant VP1 G–H loop (141–160 aa) was examined in 46 serotype O FMDV strains from Southeast Asian and Middle East–South Asian topotypes (1980–2019); single‑site (T142P, Q153P) and double‑site (T142P&Q153P) mutants were rescued using a reverse‑genetic system and introduced into an efficient FMDV nanoparticle vaccine to create four vaccine candidates.
analysis.results: VP1 positions 142 and 153 underwent sequential stepwise evolution under natural selection; mouse immunization showed solid protection against wild‑type and single‑mutant strains but markedly reduced efficacy against the double mutant; the double‑mutant vaccine elicited a neutralizing antibody titer of 1:426.67, 10–20‑fold higher than vaccines targeting wild‑type or single mutants; consistent results were observed in pigs immunized with commercial inactivated vaccines.
analysis.contribution: Combined mutations at VP1 142 and 153 reshape viral antigenicity and act as core drivers of FMDV immune evasion, providing an experimental basis for broad‑spectrum vaccine development.
analysis.limitations: Only abstract data are available; detailed methods, sample sizes, statistical analyses, and host‑specific outcomes are not reported.

analysis.summary_en: Background: FMDV evades immunity via vaccine‑driven adaptive evolution, causing breakthrough infections. Methods: Analyzed VP1 G–H loop of 46 serotype O strains (SEA and ME‑SA, 1980‑2019) and generated single (T142P, Q153P) and double (T142P&Q153P) mutants via reverse genetics, incorporating them into nanoparticle vaccine candidates. Results: Positions 142 and 153 evolved stepwise; mouse immunization protected against wild‑type and single mutants but not the double mutant; the double‑mutant vaccine induced a neutralizing titer of 1:426.67 (10‑20× higher than other vaccines); similar findings in pigs. Contribution: Demonstrates that combined VP1 142/153 mutations reshape antigenicity and drive immune evasion, informing broad‑spectrum vaccine design. Limitations: Only abstract information is provided; detailed experimental data are not reported.

title: Discovery of non-nucleoside inhibitors of the enterovirus D68 3D polymerase through crystallographic fragment and high-throughput biochemical screening

analysis.background: Enterovirus D68 (EV-D68) is a non‑polio picornavirus that has caused increasing rates of severe respiratory illness and acute flaccid myelitis in children worldwide (A1) and there are no approved vaccines or antivirals for EV-D68 (A2).
analysis.methods: The study employed crystallographic fragment screening (CFS) of 650 fragments (≈10% hit rate) and a fluorescence‑based PicoGreen high‑throughput screening (HTS) biochemical assay of 50,000 compounds targeting the EV‑D68 RNA‑dependent RNA polymerase 3Dpol (A3, A4, A6).
analysis.results: CFS identified 68 hit compounds across known and novel polymerase sites (A4); inhibition assays confirmed that binding to each site reduces 3Dpol activity (A5); HTS yielded a 5‑aminoindazole scaffold, with lead compound 727590 showing an IC₅₀ of 25 µM (A7).
analysis.contribution: The identified non‑nucleoside hits provide amenable starting points for discovery and structure‑based drug design against enteroviruses (A8).
analysis.limitations: No in‑cell or in‑vivo efficacy data are reported, and only abstract/partial text is available, so detailed methodological or safety information is not reported in the supplied evidence.

analysis.summary_en: Background: EV-D68 is a non‑polio picornavirus linked to severe respiratory illness and acute flaccid myelitis in children, with no approved vaccines or antivirals. Methods: The authors performed crystallographic fragment screening of 650 fragments (≈10% hit rate) and a fluorescence‑based PicoGreen high‑throughput assay of 50,000 compounds against the EV‑D68 RNA‑dependent RNA polymerase 3Dpol. title: Real-world influenza surveillance and vaccine effectiveness in children: a multicentre study of the Italian Federation of Primary Care Paediatricians (FIMP).

analysis.background: Influenza causes significant morbidity among children and drives primary care consultations.

title: Prevalence, incidence, mortality, and years of life lost to diabetes from 1996 to 2024 in Denmark.

analysis.background: Population‑based surveillance is essential for quantifying the burden of diabetes and monitoring temporal changes.
analysis.methods: A nationwide register‑based cohort study (1996‑2024) used an updated national diabetes register integrating hospital, prescription, clinical, and laboratory data to identify diabetes type and onset; prevalence was estimated annually with a binomial model, incidence, mortality and SMR with age‑period‑cohort models, stratified by sex and diabetes type; a multistate model assessed lifetime risk and years of life lost.
analysis.results: As of 1 Jan 2025, 366 174 individuals (6.1% of the population) had diabetes (8.2% T1D, 91.8% T2D); prevalence more than tripled since 1996, driven by an overall annual T2D increase of ~4.1%; T1D prevalence remained stable; mortality declined, especially for T1D, but excess mortality persists.
analysis.contribution: The study provides the first comprehensive, long‑term, nationwide estimates of diabetes prevalence, incidence, mortality, and years of life lost in Denmark, supporting public‑health surveillance and prevention planning.
analysis.limitations: Only abstract information is available; detailed methods, full results, and contextual data are not reported in the supplied evidence.

title: Nationwide incidence and prevalence of inherited retinal disease in Sweden, 2006-2021: a population-based register study.

analysis.background: Inherited retinal diseases (IRDs) are a rare but severe cause of vision loss on a population level. This study provides a comprehensive assessment of IRD epidemiology, including incidence, prevalence and patient characteristics in Sweden over two decades.
analysis.methods: Using Swedish national administrative registers, the study identified IRD cases (2006‑2021) and matched comparators, then calculated incidence and prevalence per 100,000 individuals standardized to the 2021 population, and compared sociodemographic and comorbidity profiles.
analysis.results: We identified 6,544 IRD prevalent cases and estimated a cumulative overall prevalence of 62.6/100 000 persons. Applying a 5‑year washout period, we identified 5,599 newly diagnosed IRD cases and estimated an overall average incidence rate of 3.4/100 000 individuals/year. Unspecified IRD accounted for over half of all prevalent cases, followed by retinitis pigmentosa‑like conditions (0.6/100 000 persons), pigment epithelial dystrophy (0.1/100 000 persons), unspecified hereditary retinal dystrophy (0.1/100 000 persons), other hereditary retinal dystrophy and vitreoretinal dystrophy.
analysis.contribution: This nationwide population‑based study provides the first comprehensive estimates of IRD prevalence and incidence in Sweden. The findings indicate a stable incidence of IRD over the past two decades. These results underscore the need for ongoing surveillance and targeted healthcare planning to address the evolving burden of IRDs.
analysis.limitations: not reported in the supplied evidence

analysis.summary_en: Background: Inherited retinal diseases (IRDs) are a rare but severe cause of vision loss on a population level, and this study provides a comprehensive assessment of IRD epidemiology in Sweden over two decades. Methods: Using Swedish national administrative registers, the study identified IRD cases (2006‑2021) and matched comparators, calculated incidence and prevalence per 100,000 individuals standardized to the 2021 population, and compared sociodemographic and comorbidity profiles. Results: We identified 6,544 IRD prevalent cases with a cumulative prevalence of 62.6/100 000 persons, 5,599 newly diagnosed cases with an average incidence of 3.4/100 000 individuals/year, and unspecified IRD accounted for over half of all prevalent cases. Contribution: This nationwide study provides the first comprehensive estimates of IRD prevalence and incidence in Sweden, indicates a stable incidence over two decades, and underscores the need for ongoing surveillance and targeted healthcare planning. title: Trends in HIV Incidence, Prevalence, Antiretroviral Therapy Coverage and Mother-to-Child Transmission Among Pregnant and Breastfeeding Women in the Eastern Cape Province, South Africa, 2000–2023

title: Prevalence, Incidence and Risk Factors for Port Site Infection Following Laparoscopic Surgery: A Multicenter Study in Bangladesh

analysis.background: Port site infection (PSI) is a significant postoperative complication of laparoscopic surgery, potentially leading to prolonged hospitalization, morbidity, and increased healthcare costs.
analysis.methods: A prospective observational study of 93 elective laparoscopic patients at Bangladesh Medical University and selected private hospitals (January 2021–December 2023) assessed PSI using CDC criteria, collecting demographics, comorbidities, operative details, and instrument sterilization practices, and applied logistic regression to identify independent risk factors.

analysis.background: Rabies is a fatal zoonotic disease; evaluating the safety of the widely used Yisheng Jun’an® freeze‑dried human rabies vaccine is essential for post‑exposure prophylaxis (PEP).

title: Establishment of the endocrine variant extractor and its clinical application in identifying a novel GATA3 mutation in HDR syndrome.

analysis.background: Genetic diagnosis of endocrine disorders is hindered by the complexity of analyzing Whole Exome Sequencing (WES) data, which generates 20,000–100,000 variants per individual, most of which are benign or of uncertain significance.
analysis.methods: The endocrine variant extractor (EVE) is a Docker-encapsulated pipeline integrating BWA-MEM, GATK, and SnpEff. It uses tiered filtering with pathogenicity scores (SIFT, PolyPhen-2) and clinical databases (ClinVar, gnomAD) across two panels: a 26-gene parathyroid panel and a 413-gene endocrine panel.
analysis.results: EVE filtered >300,000 raw variants to actionable candidates in ~3 hours, reducing manual review by >99.6%. It identified a de novo GATA3 frameshift variant (p.Ala173fs) in a Korean HDR syndrome patient, not previously reported in ClinVar.
analysis.contribution: EVE streamlines WES analysis for endocrine disorders, enabling rapid identification of novel pathogenic variants. Its open-source framework supports clinical integration of high-throughput genetic profiling and accelerates discovery of disease-causing mutations.
analysis.limitations: Sample size, population demographics, and host details are not reported. The study validates EVE on a single HDR syndrome case, limiting generalizability.

Methods: EVE is a Docker-encapsulated pipeline using BWA-MEM, GATK, and SnpEff with tiered filtering. title: Incidence and factors associated with premature ovarian insufficiency: a population-based cohort study

analysis.background: The study investigates the incidence of premature ovarian insufficiency (POI) and its associated factors in Ontario, Canada, between 1995 and 2019, addressing a condition with a global prevalence of ~3.7% and rising rates.

title: The association between artificial light at night and inflammatory bowel disease incidence, surgery, and health services utilization: population-based observational studies.

analysis.background: The urban environment increases the risk of inflammatory bowel disease (IBD), but specific environmental exposures remain unknown.

analysis.results: Among 3,929,374 individuals in the birth cohort, 5,539 (0.1%) developed IBD; no association between ALAN at birth and IBD was observed (35–60: HR 1.03, 95% CI 0.87–1.22; >60: HR 0.93, 95% CI 0.78–1.11). analysis.limitations: The study is limited to an abstract‑only report, lacking detailed methodology and contextual information, and the authors note that additional research is needed to understand ALAN’s impact on IBD.

title: Economic evaluation of including the EV71 vaccine in the national immunization program: a modeling study in Guangxi, China.

analysis.background: Hand, foot, and mouth disease (HFMD) is a major public health issue in China, particularly among children under 5 years. Enterovirus 71 (EV71) causes severe cases and mortality, but vaccines are currently self-paid, limiting access.
analysis.methods: A decision tree-Markov model simulated 420,000 newborns in Guangxi over 5 years, comparing free EV71 vaccine inclusion in the National Immunization Program (NIP) versus self-paid vaccination. Cost-effectiveness (ICER) and cost-benefit (BCR) analyses were conducted.
analysis.results: NIP inclusion increased vaccination by 344,190 individuals, prevented 14,234 HFMD cases and 16 deaths, and yielded 1,260.8 additional QALYs. ICER was USD 8,319.99/QALY (1.005× per capita GDP), with a BCR of 0.515. Vaccine price was the most influential parameter.
analysis.contribution: The study demonstrates that publicly funded EV71 vaccination in Guangxi is cost-effective and reduces HFMD burden. Price reductions could achieve cost-benefit balance, informing policy decisions in China and similar settings.
analysis.limitations: The model-based analysis assumes regional-specific data and does not account for potential real-world variability. Generalizability beyond Guangxi is limited, and long-term outcomes are not evaluated.

analysis.summary_en: Background: HFMD is a major public health issue in China, with EV71 causing severe cases. Methods: A model evaluated 420,000 newborns in Guangxi over 5 years, comparing free EV71 vaccination vs. self-paid. Results: Free vaccination prevented 14,234 cases, 16 deaths, and 1,260.8 QALYs, with an ICER of USD 8,319.99/QALY. Contribution: Publicly funded EV71 vaccination is cost-effective in Guangxi, supporting policy decisions. Limitations: Model-based and region-specific.

title: AIVA: An Agentic Platform for Phenotype-Aware Variant Analysis, Interpretation and Clinical Decision Support in Rare Disease

analysis.background: Rare disease diagnosis remains slow, with patients facing a diagnostic odyssey averaging 5 to 7 years.
analysis.main_directions: The review focuses on shifting the bottleneck from sequencing to interpretation, highlighting limitations of current classifiers, the need for phenotype‑aware prioritization, and the introduction of an agentic platform (AIVA) that integrates real‑time literature retrieval and ACMG/AMP classification.
analysis.current_state: AIVA achieved a macro F1 of 80.5% on 8,387 ClinGen‑curated variants, outperforming rule‑based classifiers, and ranked causal genes first in 66.7% of 1,396 simulated cases, while also detecting and correcting assembly errors.
analysis.gaps: Existing tools still rely on manual literature curation and generic ACMG rules, limiting automated pathogenicity assessment, and lack mechanisms to self‑correct input errors.
analysis.future_research: Future work should validate AIVA across diverse clinical settings, expand its integration of functional data and VCEP specifications, and assess its impact on reducing diagnostic timelines.

title: Prolonged coma and cerebral oedema in a patient with an ATP1A2 variant.

analysis.background: ATP1A2 encodes the α2 subunit of Na+/K+-ATPase and is associated with familial hemiplegic migraine type 2, epilepsy, and intellectual disability.
analysis.methods: A case report of a 22-year-old woman with intellectual disability, hemiplegic migraine, and epilepsy who developed prolonged coma and cerebral oedema. An epilepsy gene panel identified an ATP1A2 variant.
analysis.results: The patient had two episodes of cerebral oedema; genetic testing revealed a likely pathogenic ATP1A2 variant (c.1027A>C, p.(Thr343Pro)). Memantine treatment reduced migraine and seizure frequency.
analysis.contribution: This case underscores the value of early genetic testing in epilepsy to identify ATP1A2 variants and guide targeted therapies like memantine.
analysis.limitations: Limited to a single case report; no population or comparative data reported.

analysis.summary_en: Background: ATP1A2 variants are linked to neurological disorders. Methods: Case report of a 22-year-old with epilepsy and cerebral oedema; genetic testing identified an ATP1A2 variant. Results: Cerebral oedema resolved after memantine treatment reduced seizures and migraines. Contribution: Highlights genetic testing for targeted epilepsy management. Limitations: Single-case report with no population data.

title: Genetic structure of Rattus rattus populations in an endemic plague focus in Madagascar: Implications for rodent surveillance and management.

analysis.background: Plague remains a major public health concern in Madagascar, with Rattus rattus as the main reservoir of Yersinia pestis in the Central Highlands. Understanding rat population dynamics is critical for effective control strategies.
analysis.methods: Sampling occurred in six villages in the Azobenzene district, both inside houses and in outdoor habitats, in 2019 and 2020. 480 R. rattus individuals were genotyped at 18 microsatellite loci.
analysis.results: Genetic diversity was similar across villages and years. Outdoor subpopulations showed higher diversity and lower differentiation than indoor subpopulations, indicating larger effective population sizes outdoors. Overall low differentiation suggested extensive rat dispersal at the district scale.
analysis.contribution: Findings highlight the need for integrated plague control combining indoor flea management and outdoor human-rodent contact reduction, as local rodent control alone may fail due to rapid recolonization.
analysis.limitations: The study focused on a single district and two years; generalizability to other regions or timeframes is not reported. Host-specific transmission dynamics are not directly addressed.

analysis.summary_en: Background: Plague in Madagascar relies on Rattus rattus as a reservoir. Methods: 480 rats from six villages were genotyped in 2019-2020. Results: Outdoor subpopulations showed higher genetic diversity and lower differentiation than indoor ones, with low overall differentiation. Contribution: Integrated control strategies are needed due to rapid recolonization. Limitations: Single-district focus and limited timeframe.

title: Prevalence and predictors of abnormal cervical cytology among women living with HIV and without HIV from the MACS/WIHS combined cohort study.

analysis.background: Cervical cancer incidence has declined in the U.S., but the impact of HIV and immunosuppression on cervical abnormalities in the ART era remains unclear.
analysis.methods: A cross-sectional analysis of 1,643 women (29–74 years) from the MACS/WIHS cohort used first Pap smears (2020–2024) to compare HIV-positive and HIV-negative women via statistical tests and logistic regression.
analysis.results: 86.5% had normal cytology; 8.0% ASCUS, 4.8% LSIL, and 0.7% high-grade lesions. HIV-positive women with CD4 <200 cells/μL had higher odds of ≥ASCUS (adjusted OR not reported). HIV status, low CD4, prior abnormalities, and smoking predicted ≥ASCUS.
analysis.contribution: Identifies HIV, immunosuppression, and behavioral factors as key predictors of cervical abnormalities, informing targeted screening for WLWH.
analysis.limitations: Cross-sectional design limits causal inference; no data on ART adherence, HPV status, or geographic location.

analysis.summary_en: Background: Cervical cancer incidence has declined, but HIV's role in cervical abnormalities remains unclear. Methods: Cross-sectional analysis of 1,643 women (MACS/WIHS) using 2020–2024 Pap smears. Results: 86.5% normal cytology; HIV-positive women with CD4 <200 cells/μL had higher abnormal cytology. Contribution: Highlights HIV, immunosuppression, and smoking as risk factors. Limitations: Cross-sectional design; missing ART adherence and HPV data.
